title: Why Do We Need Cryptography? 🌍
description: From credit cards to messaging apps, cryptography is the invisible shield protecting your digital life.

slides.title: The Internet Is a Public Place 🏞️
slides.content:
When you send a message, it bounces through dozens of routers. Without protection, **anyone along the path can read it**.

Think of it like shouting your bank password across a crowded room – not a good idea!

Cryptography turns that shout into a scrambled noise that only the person with the right “ear” can decode.

slides.title: Four Pillars of Security 🏛️
slides.content:
Modern cryptography provides these essential guarantees:

1. **Confidentiality** – Only intended recipients can read the message.
2. **Integrity** – The message hasn’t been altered in transit.
3. **Authentication** – You’re really talking to who you think you are.
4. **Non‑repudiation** – The sender cannot deny having sent the message.

Every time you see `https://` or use WhatsApp, these pillars are at work.

quizData.question: Which pillar prevents a hacker from changing your bank transfer amount?
quizData.explanation: Integrity ensures the message has not been tampered with. Confidentiality hides it, but doesn’t detect changes.

slides.title: Real‑World Scenarios 🌉
slides.content:
**E‑commerce:** When you buy shoes online, encryption hides your credit card number. Without it, anyone on the same Wi‑Fi could steal it.

**Messaging:** End‑to‑end encryption (like Signal) ensures that even the service provider cannot read your chats.

**Software updates:** Code signing guarantees that the update came from the real developer, not a hacker injecting malware.

**Blockchain:** Cryptographic hashes link blocks together, making tampering nearly impossible.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🛡️
slides.content:
## Look for the Lock

Always check for the padlock icon 🔒 in your browser’s address bar. It means the site uses TLS (Transport Layer Security) – a cryptographic protocol that protects your data in transit.

quizData.question: End‑to‑end encryption in WhatsApp protects which pillar the most directly?
quizData.explanation: End‑to‑end encryption ensures only the sender and receiver can read the message – that’s confidentiality. It doesn’t directly prove who sent it.
